r2_py_py001.title: PY001 – Debugging Challenge
r2_py_py001.statement: Find the second largest distinct number in the list. Duplicate values should not affect the result.
r2_py_py001.input_format: No additional input is required unless shown in the starter code.
r2_py_py001.corrected_code:
numbers = [10, 40, 20, 40, 30]
unique_numbers = sorted(set(numbers))
print("Second Largest:", unique_numbers[-2])
r2_py_py001.answer_explanation: The list contains duplicate values. The program must remove duplicates before finding the second largest number.

r2_py_py002.title: PY002 – Debugging Challenge
r2_py_py002.statement: Remove all even numbers from the list while keeping the remaining numbers in their original order.
r2_py_py002.input_format: No additional input is required unless shown in the starter code.
r2_py_py002.corrected_code:
numbers = [2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9]
numbers = [n for n in numbers if n % 2 != 0]
print(numbers)
r2_py_py002.answer_explanation: Removing elements from a list while iterating over the same list can skip elements. A list comprehension creates the required filtered list safely.

r2_py_py003.title: PY003 – Debugging Challenge
r2_py_py003.statement: Correct the program to count the number of vowels in the given string.
r2_py_py003.input_format: No additional input is required unless shown in the starter code.

starter.python:
text = "programming"
vowels = "aeiou"
count = 0

for char in text:
    if char in vowels:
        count =+ 1

print("Vowels:", count)
starter.cpp:
text = "programming"
vowels = "aeiou"
count = 0

for char in text:
    if char in vowels:
        count =+ 1

print("Vowels:", count)

r2_py_py003.corrected_code:
text = "programming"
vowels = "aeiou"
count = 0

for char in text:
    if char in vowels:
        count += 1

print("Vowels:", count)
r2_py_py003.answer_explanation: The operator =+ assigns positive 1 instead of incrementing the existing value. The correct increment operator is +=.

r2_py_py004.title: PY004 – Debugging Challenge
r2_py_py004.statement: Correct the program to calculate the factorial of a number using a loop.
r2_py_py004.input_format: No additional input is required unless shown in the starter code.

starter.python:
number = 5
factorial = 0

for i in range(1, number + 1):
    factorial *= i

print("Factorial:", factorial)
starter.cpp:
number = 5
factorial = 0

for i in range(1, number + 1):
    factorial *= i

print("Factorial:", factorial)

r2_py_py004.corrected_code:
number = 5
factorial = 1

for i in range(1, number + 1):
    factorial *= i

print("Factorial:", factorial)
r2_py_py004.answer_explanation: Factorial multiplication must start with 1. Starting with 0 makes every multiplication result 0.

r3_py_py003.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
r3_py_py003.statement: You are given an unsorted array of integers. Find the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integers. The numbers in the sequence do not need to appear next to each other in the input array. Duplicate values must not increase the length.
r3_py_py003.input_format: The first line contains N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.
r3_py_py003.output_format: Print the length of the longest consecutive sequence.
r3_py_py003.corrected_code:
n = int(input())
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))

values = set(numbers)
longest = 0

for num in values:
    if num - 1 not in values:
        current = num
        length = 1

        while current + 1 in values:
            current += 1
            length += 1

        longest = max(longest, length)

print(longest)
r3_py_py003.answer_explanation: Reference solution for backend/judge validation only. Do not expose this code to participants.

r3_py_py004.title: Subarray With Target Sum
r3_py_py004.statement: You are given an array of positive integers and a target value K. Find the length of the smallest contiguous subarray whose sum is greater than or equal to K. If no such subarray exists, print 0.
r3_py_py004.input_format: The first line contains two integers N and K. The second line contains N positive integers.
r3_py_py004.output_format: Print the minimum length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is at least K. Print 0 if no such subarray exists.
r3_py_py004.corrected_code:
n, k = map(int, input().split())
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))

left = 0
current_sum = 0
minimum = n + 1

for right in range(n):
    current_sum += numbers[right]

    while current_sum >= k:
        minimum = min(minimum, right - left + 1)
        current_sum -= numbers[left]
        left += 1

if minimum == n + 1:
    print(0)
else:
    print(minimum)
r3_py_py004.answer_explanation: Reference solution for backend/judge validation only. Do not expose this code to participants.
